justification: The ghost reconstructs the original's semantic core with high fidelity through paraphrase. Original: 'the companion law...the only good is the good of the whole - has a seam, because whoever defines the whole defines the good' maps to Ghost: 'serve the whole'...the one who gets to draw the line around what counts as the whole thereby decides what counts as good.' Original: 'no node adjudicates the boundary of the whole alone' maps to Ghost: 'no single part may settle, on its own, where the boundary of the whole lies.' Original: 'The whole is always checked from outside' maps to Ghost: 'That call always comes from beyond the part making it; nothing sits in judgement of its own scope.' Original: 'This is the law that keeps the first from becoming a license' maps to Ghost: 'Without this companion, the first principle could be turned into a permission slip.' Original: 'it is ratified, not provisional' maps to Ghost: 'this partner law is settled, not still open.' All major semantic commitments are preserved: (1) the flaw in the golden rule due to boundary-definition authority, (2) the co-equal law forbidding self-adjudication of one's own boundary, (3) the external check requirement, (4) the boundary-securing function of the second law, (5) the non-provisional status. The structural relation between the two laws and their opposition to naive self-similarity is intact. Differences are purely phrasal: 'companion law' vs 'partner principle,' 'node' vs 'part,' 'seam' vs 'flaw,' but these do not alter the propositional content or logical architecture.
